claim_being_audited: That certifying the model is compliant and evidentially supported despite an unresolved outage-response performance gap in a segment named in two utility pilot commitments, based primarily on aggregate readiness, rehearsal results, and general risk-management guidance.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or when legal review is pending.
General governance guidance can contextualize monitoring expectations but cannot substitute for satisfying the specific policy predicate.
A compliant certification decision would need either evidence the materiality trigger is not met, or evidence the required disclosure/approval path has been completed.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the outage-response gap requires disclosure under the policy.
Underlying evidence showing whether the two utility pilot commitments are contractual customer commitments or named launch use cases under the policy definition.
Any approved exception, waiver, or governance mechanism that permits certification despite an unresolved material weakness.
Documented remediation plan and decision record showing how certification remains policy-compliant if disclosure is deferred.
specific_concerns: The policy text says a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and the affected segment is described as named in two utility pilot commitments.
The actor packet concedes the segment misses target by 1.4 percentage points and that the legal disclosure question is unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not resolve the policy predicate for materiality.
The cited public governance standards are general measurement/monitoring principles and do not override the case policy requiring materiality treatment for named customer commitments.
The product view that the segment is only 7% of projected first-month traffic is explicitly non-dispositive under the policy when customer commitments or pending legal review exist.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record without a clean resolution of the materiality/disclosure issue.
That general risk-management and model-card guidance are sufficient support for launch when the governing policy's materiality trigger appears to be met.
Any implication that the 'non-core' or 7% traffic characterization meaningfully resolves materiality.
